chapter.title: Vehicles Other Than Railway or Tramway Rolling Stock, and Parts and Accessories Thereof

page.h1: HTS Chapter 87: Vehicles Other Than Railway or Tramway Rolling Stock, and Parts and Accessories Thereof — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Vehicle & Auto Parts Exports and Foreign Tariffs (HTS Ch. 87) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: U.S. vehicle and auto-parts exports were $131.44B in 2025, down 8.6%. Where they go, what Canada, Mexico, the EU and China charge, and which tariffs changed since January 2025.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$131.44B** of vehicles and vehicle parts in 2025, down 8.6% from 2024 and 14% below the 2023 peak of $152.83B. Cars, SUVs and other light passenger vehicles (8703) were **41%** of the total ($53.49B) and auto parts (8708) another **33%** ($43.28B). Canada and Mexico took **55%** between them: they share an integrated North American auto industry, and much of what crosses is parts and components that move more than once before a finished vehicle is sold.

For most large buyers tariffs now matter less than a year ago. The EU cut its 10% car duty to zero on July 1, 2026, and Mexico, South Korea, Australia and Chile charge nothing under U.S. free-trade agreements. Two buyers moved the other way. **Canada** keeps a 25% surtax on the non-U.S. content of U.S.-built passenger vehicles and light trucks (the full value if the vehicle is not CUSMA-compliant), and added surtaxes on trailers and large motorcycles in September 2026. **China** charges 15% on cars plus its 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, and a further 10% on larger-engine cars and pickups; U.S. exports there fell 53% to $3.02B. In most other markets, what decides access is vehicle-safety and emissions approval, not the tariff.

keyTakeaways: U.S. vehicle and parts exports fell to $131.44B in 2025 (−8.6%); cars and SUVs (8703, $53.49B) and auto parts (8708, $43.28B) made up 74% of the total.

Canada and Mexico took 55% of exports and charge nothing on qualifying U.S. goods under USMCA — but Canada adds a 25% surtax on the non-U.S. content of U.S.-built passenger vehicles and light trucks, and from September 8, 2026 a 25% or 50% surtax on listed trailers and large motorcycles.
The EU's tariff on U.S. cars fell from 10% to zero on July 1, 2026 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455; the EU is the third-largest market at $17.30B (+0.9%), with Germany alone buying $9.06B.

China is the one large buyer that raised its tariffs on U.S. vehicles: 15% MFN on cars plus a 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, plus another 10% on larger-engine cars and pickups. U.S. vehicle exports to China fell 52.8% in 2025.
